review.tdd: The evidence reports a valid first semantic RED at the real owner acceptance assertion, followed by separate assertion REDs for external .markdown publication, a seeded pre-S16 .markdown copy failing stable-ID reopen under the temporary filename workaround, diverged indexed-copy protection, expected-prior-hash enforcement, and pre-publication private diagnostics. The S16 GREEN case passes 23 assertions. Existing S15, opened registrar, and indexed-origin assertions were retained; the S15 count increased to account for the new external owner acceptance.
review.ownerAndIdentity: Real external open and renderer save-as publish a separate configured-store copy through durable intent before owner ACK. The owner assigns document identity, revision, and job. A junction lexical alias keeps a 1:N alias relationship on one document without a duplicate revision; changed content updates the same document; a hash-only alias is backfilled only by a verified source-backed reopen. A fresh owner restart preserves identity and copy bytes.
review.failureAndCompatibility: External .markdown retains its baseline .markdown contained locator, so a seeded pre-S16 alias/copy reopens and updates under the same document ID. The shared publisher permits .markdown only for opened_markdown or update with source alias provenance; save_document still requires .md. A diverged copy is protected by both registrar validation and a publisher expected-prior-hash guard. Post-publication owner failure retains the external file, copy, and replayable intent. A pre-publication destination blocker retains the external file and a bounded private retry marker. The marker is a diagnostic for later user-triggered retry, not an automatic replay job. Renderer save-as retains its existing local {success,filePath} response, with no new sourcePath or store path; external legacy markDirty was removed.
